subject: Allocation block: Greenloop remittance - hold pending VAT evidence
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@greenloop.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 08:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Payment allocation question (Greenloop)

Hi Kimberly,

Our AP team sent a single EUR bank transfer yesterday to Redwood (reference: GLP-20270501) for multiple invoices across Q1 usage. Your accounting portal shows a single unapplied credit of EUR 42,150. Can you confirm which invoices were matched?

Attached is the remittance advice we pushed to the bank (file: Greenloop_remittance_20270501.pdf). We included invoice numbers in the description but the lockbox appears to have applied the funds to invoice 3492 only (partial). We need confirmation for our month-end. Also, for the invoices raised to our EU entity we need VAT handling noted — some of these should be reverse-charge (B2B) and not include VAT.

Can you advise next steps to get the unapplied amount swept to the correct invoices?

Thanks,
Oliver
Head of Finance
Greenloop Analytics

<attachment: Greenloop_remittance_20270501.pdf>

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@greenloop.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 09:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Payment allocation question (Greenloop)

Hi Oliver — thanks for the remittance.

Short answer: we see the incoming wires and the unapplied balance; it landed in a suspense account because the lockbox only matched invoice 3492. I can coordinate the sweep to apply the remaining EUR 36,750 to the outstanding invoices, but we need documentation for the VAT/reverse-charge for the EU entity before we can change the tax tags on those invoice records.

Next steps I propose:
- Please confirm which of the invoice numbers on the remittance are EU-entity invoices that should be reverse-charged (list the invoice IDs).
- If available, attach the Purchase Order or VAT registration evidence for your EU entity (this speeds approvals).
- I'll open a finance ticket to sweep the unapplied credit once marissa confirms tax tagging and posts the allocation.

I'll loop in Finance (cc'ed) to validate the bank trace and schedule the allocation. If this is blocking your month-end, Rishi can flag for a one-time courtesy application while we finish compliance checks.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Revenue Ops
Redwood Inference

Subject: FW: Payment allocation question (Greenloop) -- please review hold

Marissa — forwarding Greenloop's remittance. Bank shows full EUR 78,900 posted yesterday (bank_trace attached by AP). The lockbox matched invoice 3492 only (EUR 42,150) leaving EUR 36,750 unapplied in suspense.

Key asks for Finance:
1) Can you confirm whether we can perform a manual sweep of the EUR 36,750 to the remaining open invoices for Greenloop?
2) Before changing VAT tags on existing invoices we need evidence for reverse-charge on these specific invoice IDs. Oliver said some invoices are B2B reverse-charge — see attached remittance.
3) If you can apply now, please include a ledger note and attach the bank trace to the invoice records. Provide the list of invoices you will apply to in the reply so I can share with the customer.

Attachments: Greenloop_remittance_20270501.pdf (from customer)

Thanks — Kim
Director, Revenue Ops

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 11:25:00 +0000
Subject: Re: FW: Payment allocation question (Greenloop) -- please review hold

Kimberly / Rishi,

Thanks for the heads-up. I reviewed the bank feed and Greenloop's remittance. We can clear the unapplied balance subject to 1) a clear invoice mapping from the customer or a bank trace that shows the per-invoice references and 2) VAT evidence for any invoices that require reverse-charge tagging.

What I did now:
- Initiated a provisional allocation in our AR system that places the EUR 36,750 in a pending allocation bucket (internal memo ID: AR-PEND-20270502-GLP).
- Requested a formal bank trace from Treasury; attaching interim bank trace we received (bank_trace_20270501.pdf).
- Flagged invoices 3501, 3502, 3510 as likely candidates for allocation based on balance aging and amounts.

Action for customer: please reply confirming that invoices 3501, 3502, 3510 are to be applied and whether those are EU B2B reverse-charge. If they confirm reverse-charge, attach the VAT registration (or a PO referencing VAT) and we will re-tag the invoices and complete the allocation.

If Greenloop cannot provide tax evidence quickly and this is preventing their reporting, Finance can post the allocation as a temporary non-tax-tagged application (with a memo) at the customer's request — but that requires an authorization from a sales leader (Rishi).

I've attached the bank trace we received and a screenshot export of the AR pending allocation screen. Once we get explicit confirmation, I'll push the final allocation and update the ledger.

Attachments: bank_trace_20270501.pdf; invoice_snapshot_20270502.png

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Manager, Accounts Receivable
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@greenloop.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 12:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Payment allocation question (Greenloop)

Oliver — appreciate the quick note and the remittance file.

If Greenloop confirms the invoice mapping now I will approve a temporary application of the EUR 36,750 (marked as provisional) so your month-end isn't held up, on the condition that Greenloop provides the VAT registration or PO within 5 business days for our records so Finance can finalise tax tags.

Please reply with: 1) confirmation of the invoice IDs to apply to (we think 3501 / 3502 / 3510) and 2) whether those are reverse-charge. If you can't provide VAT evidence within 5 business days we will revert the provisional allocation and move the funds back to suspense for tax remediation.

Thanks — Rishi
Head of Revenue, EMEA
Redwood Inference

Thanks team — confirmed.

We authorise the provisional application of EUR 36,750 to invoices 3501, 3502 and 3510 today. Invoice 3501 and 3502 are billed to Greenloop GmbH (DE) and should be reverse-charge B2B; invoice 3510 is billed to Greenloop UK and does include VAT. I've attached a PDF of Greenloop GmbH VAT registration and an internal PO referencing the invoice numbers (invoice_3492-vat-proof.html).

Please proceed with the provisional allocation and mark the two German invoices as reverse-charge. We'll send the formal PO via our procurement portal to your AP inbox as backup within 24 hours.

Oliver
Head of Finance
Greenloop Analytics

I posted a provisional allocation of EUR 36,750 split as: 3501 = EUR 14,500 (reverse-charge tag set), 3502 = EUR 12,250 (reverse-charge tag set), 3510 = EUR 10,000 (VAT included). Ledger memo AR-PEND-20270502-GLP updated and I attached the bank trace to each invoice record.
